label: Free 2.0
title: What 2.0 adds for everyone
lede: Surjection 2.0 can check whole journeys, show honestly what automatic tests cover, give every finding a stable id and test single components. All of it is in the MIT package.

items.title: Flows: check every step of a journey
items.text: Describe a checkout or sign-up once and the page is checked after each step. Every check shows up as its own page in the report and the baseline.

items.title: Coverage: what automatic tests can and cannot decide
items.text: See which of the 55 WCAG 2.2 A and AA criteria are tested automatically, partly, or only by a person, so a green run is not mistaken for conformance.
items.output:
# WCAG 2.2 coverage of Surjection

55 success criteria at level A and AA: 11 mostly automatic, 16 partly automatic, 28 manual only.
A passing run is no proof of conformance, not even for "mostly automatic" criteria.

| Criterion | Level | Name | Coverage | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
...
| 1.1.1 | A | Non-text Content | partly automatic | `aria-meter-name`, `aria-progressbar-name`, `image-alt`, `input-image-alt`, `object-alt`, `role-img-alt`, `svg-img-alt` |
| 1.3.2 | A | Meaningful Sequence | manual only | - |
| 1.4.3 | AA | Contrast (Minimum) | mostly automatic | `color-contrast` |

items.title: Stable ids for every finding
items.text: The results file is now version 2. Each affected element gets an id that stays the same between runs, so you can tell a new problem from a known one.
items.code:
npx surjection check --config surjection.config.json --out-json results.json

node -e "const r=require('./results.json');console.log('version',r.version,'tool',r.tool.name+'@'+r.tool.version);for(const p of r.pages)for(const f of p.findings)for(const n of f.nodes)console.log(n.id,f.rule,n.target)"

items.title: Convert old files with one command
items.text: Results files and baselines from 1.x are still read, and you can rewrite them as version 2 once.
items.outputTitle: Output (a version 1 baseline with one entry)

items.title: Component checks for Storybook and tests
items.text: Check a single component in a Storybook play function or a Testing Library test, with no Playwright needed. Page-level rules are switched off.
items.code:
import { expectAccessibleComponent } from "@sweberdev/surjection/component";

await expectAccessibleComponent(container, { name: "toolbar" });
items.output:
